recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a work group opens a new issue to change current ElementDefinition slicing semantics or to restore/maintain the retired HSPC guide artifacts elsewhere.
issue_request: FHIR-8628 reported that some HSPC slice members lacked the old ElementDefinition f:name and asked whether sliced paths should require each slice member to be named. The final Jira discussion said multiple slicing could occur in different branches, saw no broader invariant problem, and recorded fixing the erroneous Practitioner role discriminator in svn revision 6698.
initial_application: Git history contains 5fb6665151 (#8628 - fix erroneous discriminator), which changed the HSPC Practitioner spreadsheet discriminator from `Practitioner.practitionerRole.managingOrganization, Practitioner.practitionerRole.role|false|open` to `Practitioner.practitionerRole.managingOrganization|false|open, Practitioner.practitionerRole.role` in guides/hspc/practitioner-hspc-profile-spreadsheet.*.
additional_context: The old HSPC guide/profile files named by the issue are not present in the current build checkout, and exact current-source searches for hspc-provpract, hspc-servicedeliverylocation, practitioner-hspc-profile, and the bad discriminator found no active source hits. Current FHIR maps the old ElementDefinition.name to ElementDefinition.sliceName, documents that all elements following the first slicing repeat SHALL have sliceName, and still keeps sliceName optional because unsliced/common constraint entries without sliceName are valid.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the recorded discriminator correction already exists in history, the specific DSTU1 HSPC artifacts are outside current core build scope, and adding a new global invariant would be broader than the published resolution and current slicing semantics.

evidence_items.summary: Current config maps ElementDefinition.name to ElementDefinition.sliceName, and the active ElementDefinition invariant only requires sliceName when sliceIsConstraining appears.
evidence_items.learned: The f:name terminology is migrated and current optional sliceName behavior is deliberate rather than a missed FHIR-8628 fix.
